topic: Over half-term the hamster in Femi's daughter's class died, and the school quietly bought an identical one. His daughter worked it out because the new one bites. At tea tonight she asked him whether he'd do the same if she died. He has just told the table.

plan.hint: someone asks Femi a plain question about the hamster, the school or his daughter; he answers and throws in a detail nobody asked for
someone coins a short phrase for what the school did, which the others could pick up
someone grants the point just made against them, then holds their own view with a but
someone answers a direct question briefly and in the same turn hands the identical question on, minimally, by name, to someone quiet
someone other than the coiner reuses the phrase coined earlier, as a tease or as shorthand

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Hang on, how old is she? Because that's a horribly good question.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Six. She's— six and three-quarters, she'd want me to say the three-quarters. And she asked it over fish fingers, completely calm.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Over fish fingers
T.full: Over fish fingers. Course she did.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: And I said no, obviously, and she goes how would I— how would she know, because they kept the name, Nugget, same ginger, same everything, except this one bites.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Did the— the old one never bite? Not once, in what, two years of being passed round thirty children?

T.event: Rhi's elbow nudges Femi's pint towards the table edge
T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Never. Mind your pint, Rhi. Never once, and the old one had a nick out of one ear, which she's already checked the new one for.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Got it, sorry— she checked
T.full: Got it, sorry— she checked the ear?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Course she checked, it's a body double, the school's run in a body double and she's— she's doing forensics on it.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: My mum did that with budgies. Three of them, all called Raja
T.full: My mum did that with budgies. Three of them, all called Raja, and I was at medical school before my sister let on.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Three? Budgies live, what, ten years?

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: No, not— over years, Femi, years. One went, and a new Raja was in the cage by teatime, same green, and nobody, nobody in that house ever said a word about it.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: We do it with lambs. Skin the dead one and— tie the skin on an orphan, and the ewe mostly falls for it.

T.event: Jess's packet of crisps splits open across the table
T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh for— they're everywhere. Sorry, Hugh, you dress the orphan up in the dead one?
T.full: Oh for— they're everywhere. Sorry, Hugh, you dress the orphan up in the dead one? Like a little coat?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Yes. Legs through the holes.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Yeah, all right, the ewe falls for it, fine, but she's going on smell, isn't she? Mine went straight for the ear.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, but go back— you said no, obviously, and I'm not sure it is obvious. Same ginger, same name, doesn't bite. Half the parents in this town would be tempted, Femi.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Go on then

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Not in this pub, I won't.

T.event: the barman reaches in to clear the empties and goes for Jess's half-full glass
T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, that's— that's still mine. It'll have been a TA, always is, driving round pet shops with a photo on her phone.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Never the TA, it's the— the caretaker.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Would you, though, Danny?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Probably, yes. Would you, Hugh?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Me? Every collie I've had's been Fly.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: And did any of the Flys bite?

T.event: the landlord's spaniel shoves out from under the table between Hugh's boots
T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Mind your feet, that's the spaniel. Second Fly had my thumb at the show, and Will reckons she's the only real
T.full: Mind your feet, that's the spaniel. Second Fly had my thumb at the show, and Will reckons she's the only real one.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: The only real— hang on, so for Will the biter's the real one? That's, that's the exact opposite of your six-and-three-quarters, Femi.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: So the body double— the body double won, then. Will's done his forensics and he'd rather have the one that had your thumb.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: No, he— he meant real collie.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Did he, though

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: He— well. He might not've.

T.event: Femi's phone lights up face-up beside the crisps
T.speaker: Femi
T.line: That's her mum. She's still awake.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Is she still— still on Nugget?

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: No, worse, she's— she's asked her mum now, and her mum's said yes, she would
T.full: No, worse, she's— she's asked her mum now, and her mum's said yes, she would, she'd get a new one. So that's me the soft one.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Good. Honest woman, your wife.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: I had a loft out past Clun, there was a tin, a biscuit tin, and in it— four collars, cat collars, every one of them said Sooty, and the—

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Same size? The collars, were they— same size?

judgements.speaker: Femi
judgements.reason: Femi answers Hugh's question ('Never... never once') and then adds, unprompted, that the old Nugget had a nick out of one ear which his daughter has already checked the new one for, in a stretch with Hugh, Rhi and Danny all taking part.

judgements.speaker: Femi
judgements.reason: In a multi-party stretch (Hugh, Jess, Femi, Danny), Femi grants Hugh's point ("all right, the ewe falls for it, fine") and then pivots with "but" to hold their own skeptical line that the swap only works on smell and a child would check ("Mine went straight for the ear").

judgements.speaker: Danny
judgements.reason: Sunny asks 'Would you, though, Danny?', and in the same turn Danny answers briefly ('Probably, yes') then passes the identical question on by name ('Would you, Hugh?') with nothing added, in a stretch where Sunny, Danny, Hugh and Rhi are all taking part.

judgements.speaker: Rhi
judgements.reason: Rhi reuses Danny's turn-8 coinage ('body double', 'forensics') as a tease against Hugh's collie story, Jess, Hugh and Sunny are all in the exchange, and the table takes up the jab: Hugh protests (28), Sunny presses (29) and Hugh concedes (30), so the line works as common property rather than as Danny's.
